title: 1. 40 years | Personal lessons ﷺ | Seerat 2026
description:
Welcome to Episode 01 of our Seerat series. In this opening session, we explore why human life is a test of free choice and how Allah sent Prophets as living role models. We look into why the Prophet ﷺ was raised as a "brother" (Akhuhum) from within his own community, someone whose noble character and truthfulness were known to everyone around him.

We delve into his early life to see how personal loss and orphanhood were transformed into active compassion for widows, orphans, and the needy. Through his work as a merchant, we see how he demonstrated total honesty, proving that moral growth is just as important as professional success.

Discover key moments before divine revelation, including how he peacefully resolved the dangerous Black Stone (Hajar-e-Aswad) dispute. We also cover involvement in Hilf al-Fudul, an alliance formed in Mecca to fight oppression and protect the weak, and how deep distress over societal corruption led him to seek solitude in Cave Hira.

Finally, we examine the revolutionary impact of Tawheed. The message of "La ilaha illallah" freed humanity from serving worldly powers and established true equality under divine sovereignty. We close with the steadfast courage and sacrifices of early Muslims, highlighted by the martyrdom of Hazrat Sumayya (RA).

title: 5. Establish DEEN? Real meaning | اقامتِ دین کا وسیع تصور
description:
Does “Establish the Deen” mean establishing Islam at the state level? Enforcing Shariah? Creating a complete political, economic and social system? Or does the Qur’an present a broader and deeper meaning?

In **Session 5 of Quran for Guidance Today**, we explore this important question through the guidance of **Surah Ash-Shura**.

The Qur’anic command to **“establish the Deen”** is often understood in very specific political or institutional terms. But what exactly does *Iqamat al-Deen* mean in the Qur’anic context?

In this discussion, we explore:

* What does **اقامتِ دین** actually mean?
* What is the relationship between **اقامتِ دین، غلبۂ دین، and نفاذِ شریعت**?
* Does establishing the Deen necessarily mean establishing a particular political state?
* How does the Qur’an describe the collective responsibility of believers?
* What is the difference between **living by the Deen** and **establishing the Deen**?
* How should we understand this concept at the **individual, social, political and collective levels**?
* What guidance does **Surah Ash-Shura** provide for understanding the Qur’anic vision of Deen?

Rather than beginning with a preconceived political model, this session attempts to return to the **Qur’anic terminology and context** and ask:

**When Allah commands us to establish the Deen — what exactly does He ask us to establish?**

title: 4. Speaking from Heart to Heart | SOPs of Dawat
description:
How do we convey the message of Allah in a way that does not merely reach the ears, but reaches the heart?

In this session of Quran for Guidance Today, we explore the Qur’anic methodology of Dawah through the profound guidance of Surah Fussilat (Ha-Mim Sajdah), verses 30–36.

The Qur’an presents a remarkably comprehensive approach to inviting people towards Allah — beginning with the character and steadfastness of the caller, and extending to the way we respond to opposition and hostility.

In this session, we discuss:

• What does Dawah ilallah actually mean?
• Why is steadfastness essential for the one who invites others towards Allah?
• What does the Qur’an mean by “Who is better in speech?”
• How should our words and actions complement each other?
• How should we respond when our message is met with hostility or rejection?
• What does “Repel evil with that which is better” mean in practical life?
• The role of patience, wisdom and seeking refuge from Shaytan in the journey of Dawah.

This is not simply a discussion about how to preach. It is an exploration of a deeper Qur’anic question:

How can we communicate the message of Allah in a way that reaches the heart?

title: Mosquito & Guidance | Divine teaching style of Allah in Quran
description:
Quranic Parables and the Amazing Truth About the Mosquito: The Line Between Guidance and Misguidance

قرآن مجید میں اللہ تعالیٰ ایک مچھر جیسی معمولی مخلوق کی مثال کیوں دیتا ہے؟ اس ویڈیو میں سورۃ البقرہ کی آیات 26-27 کی روشنی میں اس سوال کا جواب دیا گیا ہے، اور ساتھ ہی مچھر (mosquito) کے جسم میں چھپے حیران کن scientific facts بھی بیان کیے گئے ہیں۔ اس کے علاوہ یہ بھی سمجھایا گیا ہے کہ ایمان لانے والوں اور کفر اختیار کرنے والوں کی سوچ میں کیا بنیادی فرق ہے، اور 'فاسقین' کی وہ خطرناک صفات کون سی ہیں جو خاندانوں، معیشتوں اور سیاسی نظاموں کی تباہی کا باعث بنتی ہیں

إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَسْتَحْيِي أَن يَضْرِبَ مَثَلًا مَّا بَعُوضَةً فَمَا فَوْقَهَا ۚ فَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا فَيَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِن رَّبِّهِمْ ۖ وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فَيَقُولُونَ مَاذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلًا ۘ يُضِلُّ بِهِ كَثِيرًا وَيَهْدِي بِهِ كَثِيرًا ۚ وَمَا يُضِلُّ بِهِ إِلَّا الْفَاسِقِينَ

الَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهْدَ اللَّهِ مِن بَعْدِ مِيثَاقِهِ وَيَقْطَعُونَ مَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ بِهِ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ ۚ أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْخَاسِرُونَ

بے شک اللہ تعالیٰ اس بات سے نہیں جھجکتا کہ وہ مچھر یا اس سے بھی بڑھ کر کسی چیز کی مثال بیان کرے۔ پس جو لوگ ایمان لائے وہ تو جانتے ہیں کہ یہ ان کے رب کی طرف سے حق ہے، اور رہے وہ لوگ جو کافر ہیں تو وہ کہتے ہیں کہ اللہ کا اس چیز کو مثال کے طور پر بیان کرنے سے کیا مراد ہے؟ وہ اس کے ذریعے بہت سوں کو گمراہ کرتا ہے اور بہت سوں کو ہدایت دیتا ہے، اور وہ گمراہ نہیں کرتا مگر صرف ان لوگوں کو جو فاسق ہیں؛

جو اللہ کے عہد کو پختہ کرنے کے بعد توڑ ڈالتے ہیں، اور کاٹتے ہیں اس چیز کو جس کے جوڑنے کا اللہ نے حکم دیا، اور زمین میں فساد مچاتے ہیں، یہی لوگ اصل خسارہ اٹھانے والے ہیں۔

Indeed, Allah is not ashamed to present an example — that of a mosquito or something even smaller. As for those who believe, they know it is the truth from their Lord. But as for those who disbelieve, they say, "What did Allah intend by this example?" By it He misguides many and guides many, but He misguides not except the defiantly disobedient (fasiqeen) —

Those who break the covenant of Allah after contracting it, and sever that which Allah has ordered to be joined, and cause corruption on earth. It is they who are the losers.

Surah Al-Baqarah (2:26-27)
